content: Docusate is a stool softener that works by increasing the amount of water absorbed by the stool in the gastrointestinal tract, making the stool softer and easier to pass. It is commonly used to treat occasional constipation, which may be caused by certain medications or medical conditions. Stool softeners like docusate are often the first-line treatment for preventing and managing this type of constipation. When using docusate, it is important to check the product label for ingredients, even if you have used the product before, as manufacturers may change the formulation. Additionally, products with similar names may contain different ingredients intended for other purposes. If you are self-treating with an over-the-counter product, carefully read and follow all directions on the packaging. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Docusate is typically taken orally, usually at bedtime, with a full glass of water or juice (8 ounces or 240 milliliters), or as directed by your doctor. For the liquid form, measure the dose accurately using a special measuring device or spoon. Avoid using a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. If using drops, measure the medication with the dropper provided or a dose-measuring device to ensure accuracy. This medication should only be used when needed. Do not increase the dose, take it more frequently, or use it for longer than directed. Prolonged or excessive use may lead to dependence or electrolyte imbalances. Common side effects of docusate include stomach pain, diarrhea, and cramping. Liquid or syrup forms may also cause throat irritation. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to docusate are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Before taking docusate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To prevent constipation, maintain a diet rich in dietary fiber, drink sufficient water, and engage in regular physical activity. Use docusate only for temporary relief of constipation. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store docusate at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
